title: Ephemeral KV-cache-aware Hosted Endpoints PRD & Launch Checklist
creator: Mateo Alvarez
description: Goal: Ship a coordinated PRD and launch checklist for hosted API endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) that are explicitly aware of ephemeral KV/prefix caching behavior. This PRD defines functional requirements, API compatibility constraints, rollout and canary strategy, acceptance criteria, monitoring signal thresholds, and post-launch rollback triggers. It aims to reduce costly cache misses and unexpected behavior when we introduce ephemeral cache eviction and cache-keying changes in runtime-2.4.
background: Recent runtime changes (kv eviction heuristics and adaptive prefix compression) improve throughput but change cache-key semantics in edge cases (e.g., prompt metadata or request-level flags). Consumers of hosted endpoints have observed divergent outputs in canaries when backend cache behavior differs between model variants. This PRD establishes a behavioral contract for the hosted inference surface so SDKs, Dedicated customers, and Private deployments get predictable outputs and safe fallbacks during rollout.
goals: Define API-level expectations for prefix/KV cache behavior across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Create acceptance checks and probes to detect cache-induced nondeterminism during canary runs
Provide a staged rollout plan with automated fallback to previous runtime/model variants when cache regressions are detected
Document migration guidance and developer-facing notes for customers relying on deterministic generation or cached embeddings
non_goals: Retrofitting Dedicated clusters with new hardware—this is a control-plane and runtime-behavior launch only
Guaranteeing byte-for-byte deterministic outputs across all historical model versions
requirements: R1: All hosted endpoints must expose a request header X-RW-KV-PREFIX (optional) and a response header RW-Cache-Status: HIT|MISS|STALE
R2: For chat/completions, identical inputs (prompt + prefix header + model + params) should produce outputs within defined fuzz bounds; see acceptance criteria
R3: Embeddings endpoint must include RW-Cache-Status and a cache_key hash in response metadata when the request contains deterministic flags
R4: Rerank pipeline must validate that cached embedding IDs used for similarity are compatible with new keying scheme and fall back to recompute on mismatch
R5: Console must surface cache hit-rate, per-route cache latency, and a per-route regression alert if hit-rate drops by >10% post-rollout
R6: Rollout must include synthetic probes that exercise edge cases: long prefixes, short prefixes, rapid incremental tokenization, and tool-calling metadata
api_contracts: Chat endpoint: unchanged POST /v1/chat/completions behaviorally, but accepts optional header X-RW-KV-PREFIX and returns RW-Cache-Status and RW-Cache-Key if applicable
Completions endpoint: same surface as chat; ensure streaming behavior includes final RW-Cache-Status as last metadata chunk for clients relying on SSE ordering
Embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings returns embeddings and in top-level metadata fields: 'rw_cache_status' and 'rw_cache_key' when deterministic=true

Rerank endpoint: accepts list of candidate embedding ids; on cache_key mismatch returns 409 with body { 'code': 'KV_CACHE_MISMATCH', 'detail': 'recompute_required' } unless client sets fallback_strategy=allow_fallthrough
Backward compatibility: when X-RW-KV-PREFIX is omitted, runtime must default to existing behavior; explicit prefix usage provides opt-in deterministic scoping
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Unit and integration tests cover cache headers for all four endpoints and pass in staging
AC-2: Synthetic probe suite (see probes doc link) runs in production canary lane for 72 hours with no regression alerts and <5% output divergence for generation endpoints
AC-3: Console dashboards show cache hit-rate baseline and post-deploy signals; SLO: overall cache hit-rate should not regress by >5% for low-traffic routes during canary

AC-4: Automated rollback triggers defined: 1) Average token latency increase >20% over baseline for 15m; 2) Generation output divergence >10% measured by edit-distance probe; 3) Rerank pipeline 5xx increase >1% absolute
AC-5: Customer-facing docs updated with migration notes and header contract; DevRel sign-off obtained
AC-6: Security review completed and KMS implications for cache-key logging approved
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature branch QA + integration tests (owners: ENG-runtime, ENG-api). Run synthetic probe harness locally and in CI.
Phase 1: Internal dogfood canary (10% traffic) for 24 hours against non-critical tenant group; collect RW-Cache-Status metrics and output diffs

Phase 2: Staged production canary (1 lane, 1% traffic) for 72 hours. Run automated probes that exercise edge cases and run nightly divergence scoring. If rollback triggers fire, automatically revert routing to previous runtime variant.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) over minimum 48 hours per step, with manual gate checks at each step and required sign-offs from SRE and PM
Phase 4: Wide release and documentation release; monitor 14-day post-launch threshold metrics with daily digest to stakeholders
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: rw.cache.hit_rate per-route (SLO target: 85% for common embed workloads)
Metric: token_latency.p50/p95 with labels runtime_variant and route
Alert: cache-hit-rate-drop: fires if hit_rate drops >10% relative to baseline for 30m
Alert: generation-divergence: fires if probe divergence >10% in 15m window
Alert: rerank-409-spike: fires if KV_CACHE_MISMATCH  responses increase >0.5% of requests for 15m
Runbook: SRE runbook links included; immediate mitigation includes traffic switch to previous runtime and force-recompute flow for affected rerank requests
dependencies: PM-71422 (docs: migration guide and header contract)
SEC-1201 (security review for cache_key logging and telemetry)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers relying on implicit cache-keying may see changed behavior. Mitigation: Opt-in header X-RW-KV-PREFIX and clear migration guide + allowlist for Dedicated customers to opt-out of new keying.
Risk: Embedding mismatch causing rerank failures. Mitigation: Rerank returns clear 409 with guided remediation and a fallback recompute path; add synthetic tests that simulate id drift.
Risk: Telemetry noise obscures real regressions. Mitigation: Implement guardrail baseline periods and per-route statistical smoothing before alerting.
Risk: Increased token latency for some traffic patterns. Mitigation: Canary ramp with automated rollback thresholds and the ability to divert specific routes by tag to previous runtime variant
documentation_and_customer_communication: Create a 'KV-aware endpoints' page in the Developer Docs including header reference and examples for curl/SDKs
Customer-facing migration note for Dedicated/Private tenants and a support playbook for manual migration assistance
Postmortem template prepared for any cache-induced incidents during rollout
